data.title: On Sept 12th, 'everyone was compassionate': The world needs 'to be together again' - Richard Roeill
data.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Richard Roeill, former New York Firefighter and 9/11 First Responder. His testimony reframes the legacy of September 11th not as a historical event confined to a single day, but as living history. The former New York City firefighter describes an anniversary that reactivates trauma, while the illnesses suffered by first responders make the consequences of Ground Zero ever present decades later. Yet Roeill’s testimony is not simply a narrative of sacrifice. He says that responders were misled about the dangers they faced, demanding accountability and long-term healthcare for those exposed to the very toxic air.

data.title: Kenya: Crocodiles pushed towards homes by rising lakes
data.description: Climate change is forcing Kenya's wildlife officers to go on a crocodile hunt on the shores of Lake Baringo in a bid to curb growing human-wildlife conflict. Officers are tasked with trapping the animals and relocating them — an operation as tricky as it is dangerous.

data.title: Céline Dion review – singer’s first live show in years marks a triumphant, emotional return
data.description: Plenitude Arena, Paris Dion wiped away tears and belted out the notes, giving an astounding performance despite her diagnosis of stiff person syndrome In 2022, when Céline Dion shared that she had been diagnosed with a rare incurable neurological disorder called stiff person syndrome (SPS), there was no guarantee that the 58-year-old would ever tour again. Her condition, which resulted in muscle spasms so strong that it left her with broken ribs , had made it impossible to perform, and in a 2024 documentary, I Am: Céline Dion , fans saw how the disease had constricted her once seemingly infallible voice. Through it all, though, Dion was resolute that she would one day return to the stage. “If I can’t run, I’ll walk. If I can’t walk, I’ll crawl,” she said in the film. “But I won’t stop.” Thankfully at the opening night of her sold out five-week residency in Paris, her first full-length concerts in six years, no crawling is needed: Céline Dion is back. She glides on to the stage in a black dress, an enormous diamond necklace clasped around her throat, and launches into On ne change pas. There are tears almost immediately: she struggles through the second verse, her voice cracking as she begins to cry. By the time the strum of Destin has kicked in, though, that emotion is replaced with sheer elation. “I made a promise to be back on stage. Singing for you. Singing for me,” she says. “Singing for life.” Continue reading...

data.title: Putin would rather keep killing than admit he’s lost. As a winter of misery looms in Ukraine, Nato must step in | Simon Tisdall
data.description: The Russian leader is ploughing on with his forever war – and each day is a crime against humanity. Western democracies cannot simply sit on their hands Ukraine’s people face a winter from hell. Thwarted on the battlefield, Russia is stepping up systematic, daily attacks on civilians, their homes, schools, hospitals, workplaces, and the vital infrastructure that sustains human life. Wave after wave of terrifying daytime ballistic missile and jet-drone strikes on Kyiv and other cities are destroying supermarket distribution hubs , pharmaceutical and medical facilities, logistics centres and warehouses. The result is sharply rising civilian casualties and growing shortages of food and other essentials. As a freezing winter approaches, Russia will again try to blow up Ukraine’s water supplies and power grid, cutting off electricity to millions. This is Vladimir Putin’s version of darkness at noon. He’d rather kill everybody than admit he’s lost. Russia’s leader reportedly told Donald Trump this week that his “special military operation”, now in its fifth year, was going to plan . Trump may believe him. Western analysts certainly don’t. Failing militarily and taking huge casualties , his regime is under growing domestic economic and public pressure to wind down the war. Yet Putin seems to think one last big push can finally break Ukraine’s will. Trump’s renewed meddling – after months of inertia, he sent his patsy envoys, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff , back to Moscow last weekend (they also visited Kyiv for the first time) – perpetuates Kremlin delusions of victory. Now there’s talk of more talks. And all the while, Putin kills and kills. Each day is a crime against humanity. Simon Tisdall is a Guardian foreign affairs commentator Continue reading...

data.title: Who are the 514 people accused of starting French wildfires and what motivates them?
data.description: Experts believe one-third of wildfires in France are set deliberately, with arson the biggest single cause of forest fires last year One is a boy of 15, who threw a burning cigarette into a wood near Bordeaux. Another is a 36-year-old man who set a paper bag of rubbish on fire in bushes near Perpignan. A third is a 50-year-old woman accused of lighting 17 fires south of La Rochelle. According to the French interior ministry, since the start of a summer in which a record 115,000 hectares of forest, scrub and heathland have gone up in flames, 514 people – including 198 minors – have been arrested on suspicion of starting wildfires . data.title: ‘We must slow the pace’: CEO of Anthropic calls for an AI slowdown
data.description: In a social media post, Dario Amodei proposed a plan including third-party evaluations of AI systems The CEO of the artificial intelligence company Anthropic issued a new appeal on Saturday for the AI industry to “slow down” and offered a three-part plan for doing so, saying that his company would “unilaterally” commit to the first of the steps. In a post on social media, Dario Amodei shared a link to an essay titled We Must Pace the Frontier in which he laid out how Anthropic would provide “third-party evaluators with permanent, employee-level access to our systems, so that they can verify adherence to our safety measures, report on incidents, and assess models’ alignment during training”. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Nine killed and dozens wounded in Russian strikes as Kyiv braces for harsh winter
data.description: Zelenskyy says ‘Russia wants to kill the Ukrainian economy’ as Moscow steps up attacks on infrastructure. What we know on day 1,663 Russian airstrikes killed nine people, injured dozens and damaged buildings and infrastructure across Ukraine on Saturday, as Kyiv braces for a “very difficult” winter amid intensified attacks on the country. The civilian death toll has risen sharply in Ukraine over the past two ⁠months as Russia steps up attacks ⁠on power plants and other ​infrastructure. Ukraine has hit energy facilities and warehouses in distant parts of Russia, and both sides have targeted each other’s shipping. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy, writing on Telegram, said Russia had deployed nearly 500 drones against Ukrainian targets since ⁠early morning. “Basically, the Russians have expanded the war away from the front, where they have no success, into the economy, and their tactics are as basic as it gets: destroying every site that could help people cope with the conditions of war,” he wrote. “Russia ⁠wants to kill the Ukrainian economy and break our resistance.” The city council in Kramatorsk , one of Ukraine’s frontline “fortress cities” that Russia wants to capture, ​ said Russian forces attacked private cars, killing three people in three incidents over ‌a 90-minute period . Four people were injured. “These ‌are not military targets,” the council said. “They are ordinary civilian cars. People were going about their business.” The governor of Ukraine’s Zhytomyr region, Vitaliy Bunechko, said ‌a Russian strike on a grocery store killed two people in the town of Zviahel, west of Kyiv. Bunechko said two petrol stations also came under attack. Earlier, Zelenskyy reported attacks on the south-eastern city of Zaporizhzhia and Kryvyi Rih, his home town. The governor of Zaporizhzhia region, Ivan Fedorov, said two people were killed and 11 injured in assaults on Zaporizhzhia and other localities . In Odesa region, governor Oleh Kiper said 37 people, including an infant, were injured in a ​series of overnight attacks, while two people were missing. Russia’s defence ministry said Russian forces have maintained their strikes on Ukrainian ports, hitting a cargo ship in Odesa that it said was carrying goods ⁠for military use. Ukrainian officials said the country was bracing for a brutal winter as intensified Russian attacks on infrastructure and key export industries compound a ⁠deepening budget crisis. The economy minister, ​Oleksandr Kravchenko, said damage to infrastructure and fixed assets from Russian airstrikes was estimated at close to $10bn this year, while the broader economic costs of the attacks and ⁠the de facto blockage of its ports had cut 1.5 percentage points of GDP. “We anticipate a very difficult winter in terms of both critical infrastructure, which is being destroyed every day ⁠by Russian attacks, but also in terms of overall economic conditions in the country,” he said. With fighting on the frontline largely stalled, Russia and Ukraine have increasingly ‌targeted logistics networks and other economic assets in an effort to undermine each other’s war effort . For more than two weeks, Russia has carried out near constant attacks on Kyiv using faster j et-powered drones , disrupting life, business and government operations. Moscow has also effectively blocked Ukraine’s Black Sea ports by intensifying its air attacks on the country’s southern regions. Ukraine’s ‌main exports – agricultural products and iron and steel – are shipped via these ports. In Moldova on Ukraine’s western border, authorities closed national airspace for nearly an hour after a drone was detected near the border. Seven border crossings were temporarily closed. Zelenskyy said he would be willing to meet Putin at the G20 summit in Miami for talks on ending the war, in a media interview released Saturday, but the Kremlin immediately ruled it out. “It is impossible,” Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told AFP in New Delhi on Saturday, repeating Moscow’s demand that a meeting can only take place in the Russian capital. The gathering of world leaders takes place on 14-15 December and there has been no confirmation yet as to whether Putin would attend. Putin has repeatedly rejected offers for a face-to-face meeting with Zelenskyy. Continue reading...

data.title: Elena Rybakina beats Aryna Sabalenka to seal dramatic US Open title triumph
data.description: Rybakina wins 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 despite first-serve problems Overcomes top seed and two-time defending champion Even after she had won grand slam titles and conquered all surfaces, Elena Rybakina has always been considered lesser than the greatest players of her era. She has long been one of the most devastating shotmakers in the world, but there were always a couple more consistent and mentally tougher players above her. She leaves New York, finally, as the undisputed best tennis player on the planet, the new standard bearer of the women’s game, after following up her snatching of the No 1 ranking from Aryna Sabalenka by succeeding her as the US Open champion. As she has done throughout this unforgettable week, the Kazakhstani showed her toughness in another spectacular tussle with her great rival, nervelessly closing out a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory over Sabalenka, the top seed and two-time defending champion. Continue reading...

She leaves New York, finally, as the undisputed best tennis player on the planet, the new standard bearer of the women’s game, after following up her snatching of the No 1 ranking from Aryna Sabalenka by succeeding her as the US Open champion. As she has done throughout this unforgettable week, the Kazakhstani showed her toughness in another spectacular tussle with her great rival, nervelessly closing out a 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 victory over Sabalenka, the top seed and two-time defending champion. data.title: Making Iraq ‘normal’ again: do mass arrests and cash seizures signal end to corruption?
data.description: Government insiders say the new PM is unleashing an ‘earthquake’ to clean up the system. But Iraqis have heard it all before The gates of the Green Zone in Baghdad are made of five-metre-high armoured steel, reinforced with horizontal girders, and strung between concrete pillars and anti-blast walls. Police water cannon trucks are stationed nearby, along with armoured personnel carriers and squads of heavily armed soldiers. At the first sign of street protests – over failing electricity, unemployment or, more recently, the US-Israeli attacks on Iran – the gates are shut. X-shaped vehicle barriers, made from welded iron beams and mounted on wheels, sit ready at the roadside alongside coils of razor wire; both are slid across the street, sealing off the sprawling neighbourhood, home to the presidential palace, parliament, the prime minister’s office, the massive fortress-like US embassy, and other institutions, including the homes of scores of politicians and members of parliament. Continue reading...

data.title: My partner’s sister has published a family memoir that's unfair to him. Should we cut ties? | Ask Annalisa Barbieri
data.description: She should have been much more careful, but everyone has their own version of the ‘truth’. Does your partner want a reconciliation? My sister-in-law wrote and published an emotionally charged “memoir” of family dislocation and trauma, in which she massaged the truth of her family’s past to portray my partner as emotionally damaged . ( In fact, he is empathetic and was beloved by those he worked with.) Theirs was a complex family story , and there were many omissions and mis truths, which she failed to factcheck with us . She tried to de‑identify her brother, but he would be recognisable to anyone with a rudimentary ability to search the internet. Legal action was considered, but decided against. Who gets to tell a story in these times? Whose story is more “true ”? And should we cut off all ties or attempt reconciliation? Continue reading...

data.title: ‘You start to worry you’ll never listen to anything else’: 25 years of Can’t Get You Out of My Head, the song that saw the future of pop
data.description: Rejected by Sophie Ellis-Bextor, the minimalist dance-pop opus would become the defining song of Kylie’s career. And, a quarter of a century later, it hasn’t lost its capacity to burrow its way into your brain. La la la … Around the release of Pet Shop Boys’ 1988 album Introspective, Neil Tennant coined the term “imperial phase” to describe an era when he felt the duo “understood the essence of pop music and so we felt we could do what we liked”. For his less flowery partner in pop excellence, Chris Lowe, this was typically followed “by disappearing up your backside!”. In 2010, critic Tom Ewing fleshed out Tennant’s term by imposing three criteria : “command, permission, and self-definition”. Command related to an artist’s willingness and ability to push boundaries in a way that would reverberate through what followed. Permission, meanwhile, connected to the public and their goodwill towards an artist as they pushed things forward. Finally, self-definition, Ewing said, is the way the imperial phase defines the rest of the artist’s career. All future work will be compared with, or mentioned alongside, the output from the imperial phase. Continue reading...

data.title: A taste of home: discovering Sweden’s local food heroes
data.description: Chefs in the east of the country are shunning imported produce for local ingredients, reinforcing how food is intertwined with a region and its people ‘It’s a magical place, and not just because of the hotel.” Standing outside the greenhouses at Högbo Brukshotell , two hours north of Stockholm, Stefan Johansson is talking about far more than hospitality. The former head chef, now responsible for sustainability at Högbo, has spent much of the past decade helping reshape the way this corner of Sweden grows, cooks and thinks about food. The catalyst was disarmingly simple. Years ago, a journalist asked Johansson why he was cooking the food he was cooking. Like many ambitious Swedish chefs, Stefan trained in Stockholm’s top restaurants, where ingredients from around the world were only a phone call away. The question lingered long after the interview ended. Continue reading...

data.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother review – Mahershala Ali is a grieving hitman in soulful thriller
data.description: Toronto film festival: the two-time Oscar-winner is an unusual killer in a compelling mix of pulpy action and family drama Latif, the solemn hitman played soulfully by Mahershala Ali, carries diapers in his kill kit. I can’t tell if that’s because they come in handy when soaking up pools of blood on the fly; or because at a moment’s notice the hitman has to switch over from his brutal occupation to daddy duties. Or perhaps it’s both for this contract killer who comes armed with a blade and baby wipes, who takes lives and nurtures them, whose life is composed of jarring and poetic contradictions, much like the movie he’s in. Those contradictions are on full striking display in Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’s opening moments, an explosive close-quarters brawl in a restroom, after which Latif uses the baby wipes to clean up the mess he made with that blade. It’s a lovely image, in a film filled with so many, cutting right through the tension within this character. It also feels like a wink to the audience from Ali and writer/director Bassam Tariq, a way for them to acknowledge right off the top the distracting mess made by that other Blade. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother is premiering at the Toronto film festival and opens in select theaters in New York City and Los Angeles on 25 September, following a wider release on 2 October and 9 October Continue reading...

data.title: Solheim Cup golf 2026: final day – live
data.description: ⛳️ Solheim Cup updates from 10.10am BST at Bernardus Golf ⛳️ Live scoring | Ewan Murray’s day two report | Email Scott It was a classic matchplay double whammy. An all-timer. Yesterday evening in the gloaming , with Europe looking likely to take a 9-7 lead into the Sunday singles, Jennifer Kupcho tramlined a 90-footer on 17 before guiding in a 30-footer on the last to pull the rug spectacularly, skilfully, nervelessly, dramatically from under the feet of the astonished hosts and level the scores at 8-8. A genuine Where Were You When …? event, 120 feet’s worth of brilliance you’ll see again and again and again and again for ever more. And you can double that should the USA win and/or retain the trophy this afternoon! Take it to the bank. Jennifer Kupcho: instant Solheim Cup legend. Can Europe recover from that late, late, great bodyblow? They’ve got 12 chances to do so. They need six-and-a-half more points to regain the Solheim Cup; the USA require a mere six to retain. If the first two days are anything to go by – and Carlota Ciganda’s Seve-and-Spieth-infused heroics on Friday now seem a sepia-tinged dot in the dim and distant past in this post-Kupcho multicoloured world – this is going to be very tense, very dramatic … and an awful lot of fun. It’s on! Continue reading...

data.title: European football: Dortmund win again but Freiburg top after Gladbach rout
data.description: Milan come from behind in 2-2 draw with Lazio Kylian Mbappé strikes twice as Real Madrid cruise Felix Nmecha scored twice and Fábio Silva grabbed another as Borussia Dortmund won 3-0 at home to promoted Paderborn to continue their perfect start in the Bundesliga. Dortmund’s win made it three from three in the league this campaign, their best start in 11 seasons, dating back to Thomas Tuchel’s time. Starting up front alongside Serhou Guirassy for the first time this season, Silva converted a clever pass from the Guinean to give the hosts the lead after five minutes. Guirassy had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half but Dortmund were rarely troubled by the toothless visitors, who are yet to score since returning to the top flight. data.title: ‘I want Teófimo’: Ryan Garcia calls out rivals after two-round destruction of Conor Benn
data.description: Garcia stops Benn 1min 25sec into second round Champion floors challenger with concussive right López, Haney, Stevenson among possible fights Ryan Garcia needed less than four minutes to blow away Conor Benn before turning his sights on the rest of the welterweight division. The 28-year-old American demolished Benn inside two rounds on Saturday night to retain his World Boxing Council championship at 147lb, dropping the British challenger with a concussive right hand before the referee stepped in moments later at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas. The sensational finish ignited the mostly pro-Garcia crowd of 18,855 on Mexican Independence Day weekend. Then, with Teófimo López taunting him from ringside and threatening to storm the ring, Garcia made it clear he was ready to take on all comers. Continue reading...

data.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
data.description: ‘No wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players’ Spurs in 17th place after 0-0 draw against Everton Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home 0-0 with Everton . It is now four games in the competition since the start of the season without a goal for Spurs; they sit 17th in the table with two points and were booed off by frustrated fans. De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window. Continue reading...

data.title: Ben Shelton faces date with destiny against Zverev in US Open final
data.description: World No 4 will become the first Black American man to win the singles title at Flushing Meadow since Arthur Ashe if he can beat German for the first time As Ben Shelton lapped up the explosion of joy and adoration from a full Arthur Ashe Stadium after reaching a grand slam final for the first time, one of his first thoughts was of his paternal grandmother, Regina, who died this year. Shelton credited his grandmother with ensuring that his father, Bryan, made it as a top professional, becoming one of a small group of Black men on the tour. “My dad lost his mom earlier this year and she’s the reason he was able to play tennis,” he said. “Without her, there’s no Ben Shelton standing here today. So this one is for her.” Shelton stands on the verge of history. On Sunday, he will attempt to become the first Black American man to win the US Open singles title since Arthur Ashe in 1968, a feat he will attempt inside the stadium named after Ashe. Shelton would also be the first Black man to win any grand slam singles title since Yannick Noah at Roland Garros in 1983, and the third overall. He is also aiming to become the first American man to win a major singles title since Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003. Continue reading...

data.title: Lando Norris shocks himself by pipping Kimi Antonelli to F1 Spanish GP pole
data.description: Briton beats Antonelli by one hundredth of a second Verstappen qualifies third on tough Madring track Proving that timing is all, not least in making a statement, Lando Norris kept his very best to last for a moment that must be considered close to Formula One perfection. His pole position at the sport’s newest circuit, the Madring, for the Spanish Grand Prix was so immense it left him shocked. Not least in that he had not threatened the top of the timesheets at any point over the weekend until the final lap of the final session, and then he was masterly. On a circuit that has proved punishingly unforgiving with some major crashes, keeping it clean was vital, but for the top spot, absolute commitment and inch-perfect execution was the differentiator in threading the needle inside the looming walls of this high-speed challenge. Continue reading...

data.title: Warning: our democracy won’t survive the death of reading. Read on if you still can | John Harris
data.description: While fascists protest in UK ports and purvey nonsense and poison online,  ever fewer people have the perspective or analytical tools to challenge them Imagine this. Quite by chance, your TikTok feed presents you with footage of the fascists who recently took part in highly organised shows of strength in Dover and Portsmouth (and, on Wednesday, outside the London offices of the Daily Mail , demanding a new house for the mother of their leader, Daniel “Tommo” Thomas). For as long as the images hold your attention, you see and hear flashes of explanation, but then, as usual, you scroll away to someone leaping off a tall building, a fight on the London Underground, or a trick-performing dog. Hypothetically, TikTok users are able to skip through 260 videos in under 35 minutes . And it’s this distracted, quick-fire way that so many people receive information that may be responsible for a worrying statistic from YouGov last week . Its poll on the Dover and Portsmouth events showed that 53% of people aged 18-24 years old simply didn’t have a point of view on whether the masked demonstrations were “a legitimate way of protesting”. Further, 43% of those of all ages were either unaware of the story, or not following it at all. Continue reading...

data.title: Think of the parable of a frog in boiling water. That’s us dithering as the ‘unprecedented‘ weather becomes more extreme | Helen Pilcher
data.description: The complacency is staggering: just another hot summer, a flooded street, a crop failure. We are accepting this extraordinary deterioration as normal Recently, I overheard a conversation in a cafe where someone described their toast as “awesome”. I felt myself bristle. Not because the toast wasn’t good – I didn’t taste it – but because I remember a time when “awesome” meant something that inspired awe: towering mountains, the vastness of the night sky, the haunting song of a humpback whale. Now it’s being used to describe breakfast. “Fantastic” has met the same fate, shedding its fantastical origins to become a synonym for “great”. Meanwhile “literally” has been so thoroughly abused that it can now mean something that is, quite literally, not literal. Continue reading...

data.title: Ketchup on a Sunday roast? This is the worst thing gen Z has ever done | Polly Hudson
data.description: Swapping roast potatoes and yorkshire puddings for kimchi and avocado – how can they live with themselves? Trigger warning: the following contains a description of the most heinous abomination known to humankind. Ready? A diabolical 39% of gen Z add ketchup to their Sunday roast. This is as sacrilegious as it is unappetising. But what makes it even more appalling is that these monsters aren’t even ashamed. Instead of lurking in the shadows, hiding their Heinz, they’re happily admitting to their culinary crime in a new survey . And their misdemeanours do not end there. In news that is particularly distressing on the eve of glorious roast season, it turns out they’re also exchanging roast potatoes and yorkshire puddings for hot sauce, kimchi and – sounds like a punchline, but isn’t – literally avocado. data.title: Why is Trump’s $5,000 offer to voters ‘like a woman’? Ask Fox News | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: Host Jesse Watters says Trump’s offer to Americans if Republicans retain Congress is ‘an enticement’, not a bribe I think I finally understand why Fox News pays Jesse Watters the big bucks. The network star, famous for hot takes like men shouldn’t “eat soup in public”, has an incredible talent for inserting misogyny into absolutely any news story. Take, for example, Donald Trump’s ludicrous announcement on Wednesday night that he will give every American adult $5,000 if Republicans retain control of the US Congress in November’s midterm election. That’s a story about apparent bribery, right? A story about fiscal recklessness and empty promises. A story about how the president, whose popularity is plummeting, is so out of ideas that he’s resorted ( yet again ) to dangling cash in front of voters. Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

data.title: Religious Vance seeks to avoid Maga schism as he keeps the faith for 2028
data.description: Vice-president wears religion on his sleeve but winding spiritual path could alienate evangelicals and Catholics US vice-president JD Vance has worn his religion on his sleeve since converting to the Catholicism in 2019. He recently published a book, Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith, and memorably met the late Pope Francis at the Vatican on Easter Sunday in 2025, a day before the pontiff died. But his religious identity could take on new weight as he positions himself for a presidential run in 2028, in which a successful campaign would make him only the third Catholic president in US history. Vance’s winding spiritual path – combined with his avowed evangelical roots – have the potential to stymie him, as he seeks to retain the Christian nationalist voters that have sustained Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again (Maga) movement while wooing fellow Catholics. data.description: As trust in institutions wavers, experts say local, collective action is more effective in driving change Wildfires, excess deaths, hosepipe bans, school closures: this summer many British people have experienced the often devastating effects of the climate crisis in ways they had not before. This week, reflecting on a summer as “hot as hell” , the UN’s head of climate, Simon Stiell, said: “Climate is sometimes seen as a partisan issue, as territory in the culture wars. That is palpably false.” Continue reading...

data.title: Misty Green review – Chris Rock’s jumbled LA drama saved by fiery Rosalind Eleazar
data.description: Toronto film festival: There’s a stunning lead performance from the breakout British actor but the film surrounding her can’t quite match what she’s bringing There’s a mighty, all-guns-blazing performance at the centre of Chris Rock ’s cynical Hollywood-set spiral Misty Green, a spark of fire almost put out by the relative dampness of the film surrounding. British actor Rosalind Eleazar, best known for her work in Slow Horses , has probably vaulted herself into a strangely underpopulated best actress race with her turn as a struggling actor trying to grapple her way back to the middle. Eleazar does enough here to go much higher. Misty has an Emmy for her role on still beloved TV series Red Eye but it sits on the shelf of an apartment paid for by a married, and recently deceased, benefactor, right next to the empty liquor bottles and a rolled-up bill used for last night’s cocaine. The film throws us into her final week there, as a brittle, short-tempered widow (Amy Landecker) gives her seven days to find somewhere else to live, not easy in a city like LA and even harder when she’s unable to find work. Her lack of employment is both a result of an industry that doesn’t have a place for someone like her (she’s “too black to be with Leo, not black enough to be with Damson, not a nepo baby and not a Brit”) and also her difficult temperament, stuck in a “one-sided beef with Shonda” and choosing wild, drug-fuelled nights over bright-eyed morning auditions. Misty Green is premiering at the Toronto film festival and is out in US cinemas on 9 October and will premiere at the London film festival in October with an Australian release to be announced Continue reading...

data.title: Girl Group review – Rebel Wilson’s dreadful music comedy is a spice-free wannabe
data.description: Toronto film festival: the actor turned writer-director’s ode to girl groups is a shoddily made and embarrassingly unfunny catastrophe There were plentiful on-paper delights for certain music fans of a certain generation promised at Toronto’s splashy Friday-night premiere of pop comedy Girl Group. Posed as a tribute to the Spice Girls and the fizzy boom of girl power-fuelled music that came in their wake, its cast includes OG member Mel C, All Saints’ Shaznay Lewis, and Pussycat Dolls’ Ashley Roberts and Nicole Scherzinger while its soundtrack includes Glee-like covers of Destiny’s Child, En Vogue and Fifth Harmony, a feast for those who have recently felt famished. At a time when such music is still sadly rather thin on the ground, save for the manufactured kids pop of Katseye and the often effective yet more boutiquey throwback R&B of Flo, it seemed to be a reminder of how thrilling it all used to be back when such girl-pop supremacy felt impossibly never-ending, a form of nostalgia-bait that many of us could fully get behind. But there are not enough pandering nods to the past that will get even the most dedicated pop girlie through the five-alarm catastrophe that unfolded for those of us who bravely decided to stay awake (someone in front of me wisely chose the release of sleep within the first 30 minutes). Hailing from Live Nation Studios, also behind the Weeknd’s roundly ridiculed vanity project Hurry Up Tomorrow , but lit and shot like a pharmaceutical commercial, it barely even feels like a real movie let alone one that should be premiering at such a prestigious festival. It’s the clumsy handiwork of Rebel Wilson, a once in-demand comedy star who has been trying to chase her career highs in the years since. In a theoretically admirable move, she’s moved behind the camera to take control and reintroduce the kind of broad comedies she used to be a part of before they faded from the mainstream. Her directorial debut, a cheap and cheerful adaptation of Australian stage musical The Deb , was ultimately best known for being the subject of a nasty and prolonged court case , but it showed us how Wilson saw herself as a film-maker and which of her films she was most eager to relive *coughs* Pitch Perfect *ends cough*. Girl Group sees her return once again to that territory – female friendship, musical numbers, unfriendly competition – but with even lesser results. Girl Group is premiering at the Toronto film festival and is seeking distribution Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I grew my hair and dropped out of society after hearing Black Sabbath’: J Mascis’s honest playlist
data.description: The Dinosaur Jr axe man stole from his mum to buy a Beach Boys record and squeaks to Tom Petty – but which punk banger made him cry? What’s the first song you fell in love with? Monster Mash by Bobby “Boris” Pickett. Monsters appealed to me as a kid. I found it funny, not spooky. Since I had a kid, Halloween has become the biggest holiday of the year. What was the first single you bought? I bought Darlin’ by the Beach Boys with the money I would steal from my mom. I always liked the Beach Boys. I remember they were quite unhip for a while: I played them at a gig around 1989 before we came on and people hated it. Now they’ve become more hip again. Continue reading...

data.title: Eurovision made me realise that I was autistic at 34
data.description: I had always dreamed of attending the song contest. But all that glitter brought on sensory overload – and I finally understood who I actually was The Eurovision song contest meant a lot to me growing up. The eclectic performances. Terry Wogan’s despair. The yearly tradition of Greece giving “douze points” to Cyprus and Cyprus giving “douze points” to Greece. The hedonistic, unpredictable event playing out on my bedroom television couldn’t be further away from the idyllic yet conservative Dorset I grew up in. Most of my youth consisted of trying to work out how to perfectly align my future career so I could work at the contest if it ever ended up in the UK again, all while being confused by why my friends were not interested in my written analyses on each entrant. Continue reading...

data.title: Julia Donaldson: ‘Am I the Gruffalo Granny? Not really. I’m the mouse’
data.description: As she introduces the latest member of her Gruffalo family, Julia Donaldson talks about storytelling, loss and the worries that come with being Britain’s all-time bestselling author In 1999 a journalist asked a then-unknown author to share her millennium wish. The author, who was 51 years old and had published only one book before, said she hoped her new one, out that year, would become a classic. “But then straight away I said: ‘Only joking!’ Because I didn’t want to sound full of myself, and I certainly didn’t think the wish would come true,” she remembers today. That author is Julia Donaldson; the book she published in 1999 was The Gruffalo; and, as you hardly need telling, her wish did indeed come true. And how. Since its publication, more than 18.2m copies of The Gruffalo and its sequel have sold worldwide. The Gruffalo’s Child was published in 2004, and together these tales of the terrible creature with terrible claws, and terrible teeth in his terrible jaws, have helped Donaldson to sell more than 50m books in the UK. In 2025 she was named the country’s bestselling author – across all genres, children’s and adult’s – since records began. Continue reading...

data.title: Deepfakes are wrecking influencers’ credibility, one fake ad at a time
data.description: Influencers aren’t just battling competitors for brand deals. They’re now battling AI versions of themselves Earlier this year, Emily Schuman, the creator of the lifestyle blog Cupcakes and Cashmere, saw a photo of herself she didn’t recognize on Instagram. In a sponsored ad, Schuman, who has more than 500,000 Instagram followers, is holding up a vial of GLP-1 drugs, advertising the telehealth company Gala. There was just one problem: Schuman had never heard of Gala and had nothing to do with the ad. The ad was based on a digitally altered version of a selfie Schuman had taken in her car and posted on Instagram years earlier. Once her followers got wind, they flooded her inbox with questions about the sponsorship as it didn’t seem consistent with Schuman’s personal brand. Soon after, Schuman discovered this was just the beginning. There was also an Instagram post where an AI version of her with darker hair appears to apply foundation to promote a makeup brand called Meroda Cosmetics, and TikTok posts with generated images of her promoting the blood testing company Superpower. Continue reading...

data.title: I survived a stroke during an ocean swim. Here’s what I’ve learned about fear
data.description: After his stroke in rough surf, Graham Russell embarked on an unexpected journey into fear. Three lessons helped him return to the joy of the ocean Looking out over the ocean, I would watch the waves sparkling in the sunlight as they grew and spilled into a burst of froth. It was a fun way to relax, to breathe deep and enjoy an awesome display of energy. But lately it had become exhausting. In winter last year I tore the lining of an artery in my neck during a rough ocean swim off the Central Coast of New South Wales. It caused a stroke while I was in the water, which saw me scrambling back to shore where a surfer noticed me and sounded the alarm. Six months later, the injury had healed, and my motor functions were all back to normal. But as I prepared for a dip in calm conditions on a sunny day in January, I paused. An unexpected journey into fear began. Sign up for a weekly email featuring our best reads Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I love the boldness of modernism’: New York fashion week goes highbrow
data.description: Georgia O’Keeffe inspires the latest Calvin Klein while Michael Kors feels indebted to Alexander Calder Calvin Klein has taken a highbrow turn in the two years since Veronica Leoni took charge. The Italian designer, a philosophy graduate who was schooled in the chic design studios of Jil Sander and Celine, has shifted away from jeans, boxer shorts and logos, stripping the brand to its minimalist bones: slip dresses and simple coats, slim skirts and crisp T-shirts. Leoni called this the “discipline of removal”. Her muse this season was Georgia O’Keeffe, an artist who the brand’s namesake founder admired. Klein bought O’Keeffe’s painting Summer Days in 1983 for $1m, subsequently donating it to the Whitney Museum. A checked pattern taken from O’Keeffe’s distinctive capsule wardrobe of utilitarian chic appeared on this catwalk as a wrap coat, hardware-free with a fabric belt and no buttons. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘I said, if you want to fire me, just fire me. And so he did’: my showdown with Donald Trump
data.description: What’s it like to be shown the door by the US president? A former national security adviser, an Apprentice contestant and more share their stories • Plus: The truth about my 11 days in the White House, by Anthony Scaramucci Gene Folkes , 62, based in Manhattan, was a contestant on season 10 of The Apprentice , which aired i n 2010 . A former air force recruiter until 1991, he retrained as an investment banker, then launched his own business before appearing on the reality show. He was fired by Trump in episode 5 . He now runs the technology consulting firm OshunX and hosts a podcast, Folkes Unfettered . I didn’t audition to be on The Apprentice. I received the call out of the blue: “Would you be interested in doing this show?” I didn’t know a lot about it. However, like any young business person, you look for people who you consider titans. There’s this mythology around Trump. He was one of the people I wanted to emulate. Continue reading...

data.title: Beijing tightens drone crackdown, bans possession, storage across city from Nov 15
data.description: As of November 15, Beijing will officially prohibit residents and businesses from owning drones. Existing drone owners must either sell their devices or dispose of them before the deadline. Infringers will face potential confiscation of their drones along with hefty fines. This regulation enhances security measures, significantly restricting drone operations within the city, following previous limitations on unauthorized flights and the classification of all airspace as restricted.

data.title: In 2024, New York turned 250 Christmas trees into breakwaters to restore salt marsh
data.description: Discarded Christmas trees found a new purpose in Jamaica Bay, where they transformed into natural breakwaters at a wildlife refuge. The structures served to safeguard newly planted salt marsh vegetation from erosive waves. By the fall, these barriers effectively trapped sediment, partially burying themselves in the marsh. This innovative ecological restoration project showcased how recycled trees could enhance a living shoreline system, bolstering the marsh's resilience and self-protection.

He remains at the station to preserve memories as others retire.

data.title: Two giant dams starved the Danube Delta of sediment for decades
data.description: The Danube's sediment supply to its delta has significantly decreased due to upstream engineering works. Large dams like the Iron Gates trap sediment, altering the natural balance of the delta. This reduction in material has led to increased coastal erosion along the delta's seaward edge. Recently, ten obsolete dams were removed from smaller rivers to reconnect fragmented habitats.

data.title: Comment le karaoké a conquis les cœurs : « Quand j’ai commencé, on se moquait de celui qui voulait chanter du Gilbert Montagné »
data.description: Arrivé en France dans les années 1990, l’art de pousser la chansonnette en amateur et en public n’en finit pas de s’étendre en France. data.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Roumanie affirme qu’un drone s’est écrasé après avoir traversé l’Ukraine et la Moldavie
data.description: Les forces roumaines ont retrouvé, samedi, un objet volant qui s’était écrasé dans un champ de maïs près de Botosenita Mare, dans le département voisin de Suceava. data.title: Política foi a grande estrela das premiações do Festival de Veneza
data.description: Uma das grandes polêmicas do Festival de Veneza deste ano foi a escolha de apenas um filme com direção solo de uma mulher a participar da disputa pelo prêmio principal. Pois, entre os 21 longas da disputa, foi justamente ele, o dinamarquês "Woman Unknown", de May el-Thouky , o eleito para levar o Leão de Ouro, pelo júri presidido pela atriz americana Maggie Gyllenhaal . Mais que um reconhecimento estético, o prêmio é claramente uma tomada de posição -não há o que explique por que mulheres ainda hoje tenham tão mais dificuldades de participar de festivais do que cineastas homens, nos diz o júri com a premiação. E, com isso, vai na contramão do diretor do evento, Alberto Barbera, que disse que Veneza só escolhe filmes pelo seu valor estético. Leia mais (09/12/2026 - 18h22)

data.title: Så mycket har de lägre bränslepriserna kostat staten
data.description: De senaste årens skattesänkningar på drivmedel har resulterat i drygt 67 miljarder kronor i uteblivna skatteintäkter, visar DN:s genomgång. Därutöver tillkommer miljardkostnader för att kompensera för de högre utsläppen under mandatperioden. – Jag skäms inte för den politik som jag har genomfört och tänker fortsätta bedriva, säger finansminister Elisabeth Svantesson (M).

data.title: C: Stockholm måste kompenseras för höjda lönekrav
data.description: C varnar för att de skärpta lönekraven för arbetstillstånd kan slå hårt mot Stockholm. Så länge reglerna ligger fast vill C hjälpa fler att få högre lön, och kräver att staten ersätter kommunerna. Regeringen menar i stället att de nya kraven gynnar tillväxten, och att jobben som berörs kommer att kunna ersättas av arbetslösa svenskar.

data.title: Uderzenie drona 800 metrów od polskiej granicy. Rosja atakowała Ukrainę
data.description: W sześciu powiatach na terenie Lubelszczyzny zawyły syreny alarmowe w związku z zagrożeniem atakiem z powietrza – poinformował Lubelski Urząd Wojewódzki. Z powodu rosyjskich ataków na Ukrainę w nocy wstrzymane były odprawy na polsko-ukraińskich przejściach w regionie. Ok. 800 metrów od przejścia w Jagodzinie po stronie ukraińskiej dron uderzył w ciężarówkę.

data.title: Japonská firma testuje novinku. Víno bude prodávat v lahvi z papíru
data.description: Univerzita ve středním Japonsku zahájila testování papírovoplastové lahve na víno, která je zhruba o 30 procent lehčí než skleněná, s cílem snížit dopad výroby a přepravy na životní prostředí. Prodávat by se mohla od příštího roku. Nejnovější "efbottle" díky úzké výlevce a charakteristickému zúžení v horní části na první pohled vypadá jako lahev na víno, ačkoli na dotek připomíná karton na mléko.

data.title: Proč nás točená vyjde dráž než kopečková a proč tak zdražila. Věda jménem zmrzlina
data.description: Když jste si před lety chtěli v létě udělat radost, stačila vám v kapse desetikoruna. Dnes za ni nedostanete ani suchý kornoutek a cena poctivé porce zmrzliny se dotáhla na částku, za kterou jsme si ještě nedávno běžně kupovali oběd. Zmrzlina za dvě desetiletí zdražila o propastných 400 procent. Češi ji ale milují natolik, že je ani tyto cenovky od mrazicích pultů neodehnaly.

data.title: Švédi vybírají novou vládu, poprvé by v ní mohla zasednout krajní pravice
data.description: Ve Švédsku v neděli ráno začaly parlamentní volby, po kterých se poprvé na vládě může podílet krajní pravice. Očekává se těsný souboj mezi opozičními sociálními demokraty vedenými Magdalenou Anderssonovou a středopravými Umírněnými současného premiéra Ulfa Kristerssona.

data.title: V Indonésii se kvůli špatnému počasí ztratila loď, 140 lidí se pohřešuje
data.description: Záchranáři v Indonésii z lodi, kterou v Jávském moři zastihlo nepříznivé počasí, zachránili 103 lidí. Jeden z nich ale zemřel, uvedl místní šéf záchranných složek podle agentury AFP. Podle úřadů bylo na palubě lodi 243 lidí, 140 osob se tedy pohřešuje.

data.title: Litva zmizí z mapy světa. NATO zemi neochrání, hrozí Medveděv
data.description: Ruský exprezident Dmitrij Medveděv znovu sáhl k nukleárním hrozbám. Pokud by kvůli případnému rozmístění jaderných zbraní na jejím území došlo k vojenskému střetu s Ruskem, podle něj by země „zmizela z mapy světa“. Zároveň tvrdí, že NATO by v takovém případě neuplatnilo článek 5 o kolektivní obraně.

data.title: Jak „hacknout“ stárnutí. Američané hledají elixír mládí, dlouhověkost je nový trend
data.description: Za sen o věčném mládí jsou Američané ochotni platit miliony. Jedním z nových trendů  je takzvané „longevity“, tedy česky dlouhověkost. Cílem není jen dožít se vysokého věku, ale především prožít delší život bez vážných chronických nemocí.

data.title: Zemanův mutant mi udělal reklamu. Keblúšek o ČT i vstupu do politiky
data.description: Bývalý novinář Vladimír Keblúšek kandiduje za Naše Česko na Chebsku do Senátu i v komunálních volbách. Působil v ČT i na Nově, proslavil se třeba odhalením takzvané lánské schůzky a pečlivě sleduje současné dění. „Zrušení poplatků bylo nešťastné. Když už takhle rozhodli, tak měli nechat rozpočet, jaký byl plánovaný, a neškrtat žádné peníze, aby to neohrozilo projekty. V televizi se plánuje na pět až osm let dopředu,“ kritizuje.

data.title: Kabelky přímo z jeskyně. Malá dílna na Santorini láká zákazníky z celého světa
data.description: Iota Zaggleová prodává své ručně šité kožené výrobky v malém skalním výklenku na řeckém ostrově Santorini. Z nenápadného prostoru si během několika let vybudovala podnik s klientelou ve 34 zemích, aniž by spoléhala na placenou reklamu. Zákazníci ji objevují hlavně díky osobním doporučením, sociálním sítím a internetovým mapám.

data.title: Ex ji zmlátil do krve, tak se vyfotila s monoklem. A zrodila se Balada o sexuální závislosti
data.description: Své přátele fotila při divokém sexu, na záchodě, na smrtelné posteli i v rakvi. Nan Goldinová se zapsala do dějin jako revoluční fotografka newyorské umělecké scény i jako nezdolná aktivistka, která na stará kolena vytáhla do boje proti miliardářské rodině zodpovědné za opioidovou krizi. A vyhrála. Její příběh přinášíme v seriálu Slavné fotografie.

data.title: Izrael před volbami rozpoutal válku s Londýnem. Netanjahu už frustruje i USA
data.description: Izrael po britských sankcích na jeho zboží zavírá konzulát, vypovídá britské pracovníky a zakazuje vstup některým britským státníkům. Vyhrocený spor zároveň ukazuje na rostoucí napětí mezi Izraelem a některými jeho tradičními západními spojenci. Neobvykle zdrženlivě reagoval i Washington, kterému podle analytiků jednání Netanjahuovy vlády už leze na nervy.

data.title: Je nejlépe placeným voleným lídrem na světě. A teď mu ještě výrazně přidají
data.description: Post singapurského premiéra je nejlépe placenou pozicí demokraticky voleného světového lídra na světě. A současný držitel tohoto úřadu Lawrence Wong tento týden oznámil navyšování vládních platů. To znamená, že částka, která již předtím výrazně převyšovala příjmy představitelů jiných zemí, ještě naroste.

data.title: Slovesa felit nebo flexit se v jazyce uchytí, skibidi má menší šanci, říká lingvistka
data.description: Čeština se proměňuje na několika různých úrovních, vychází to i z různých komunikačních situací, které lidé zažívají, říká bohemistka z Filozofické fakulty Univerzity Karlovy Hana Dufková. Komunikace v elektronické podobě zrychluje, na mnoha místech se ustupuje od formálnosti. Ta se naopak stále udržuje v některých typech situací, jako jsou například předávání cen či promoce.

data.title: Magyar chce změnit zákon o adopcích pro stejnopohlavní páry. Za Orbána to nešlo
data.description: Maďarská vláda změní zákon přijatý v roce 2020 tehdejší vládou Viktora Orbána, který fakticky zakazoval adopci dětí stejnopohlavními páry. Oznámil to maďarský premiér Péter Magyar. V Maďarsku byla adopce homosexuálními a lesbickými páry možná do konce roku 2020, pokud jeden z partnerů podal žádost jako svobodná osoba.

data.title: Dálnici D11 zastavila hromadná nehoda. Komplikace byly v obou směrech
data.description: Dálnici D11 na 33. kilometru ve směru na Hradec Králové v sobotu kolem poledne zablokovala nehoda pěti aut, vyžádala si jedno lehké zranění. Auta havarovala v místě dopravního omezení. Komplikace byly i v opačném směru na Prahu, kudy se k nehodě dostávali policisté, hasiči a záchranáři. Provoz na dálnici se podařilo plně obnovit v 15:00.

data.title: Rusko muselo v srpnu zavřít svá letiště téměř tisíckrát. Ukrajina zvyšuje tlak
data.description: Rusko muselo za srpen zavřít svá letiště téměř tisíckrát, šlo tak o nejhorší měsíc pro civilní letectví v zemi od začátku invaze na Ukrajinu v únoru 2022. Mohou za to zejména ukrajinské drony, ruský prostor se totiž zavře při každém narušení. Ukrajinské síly pokračují v operaci Koberec, jejíž cílem je ochromit právě ruský civilní letecký provoz.

data.title: Oběma sestrám selhaly ledviny, pomohla rodina. Jedné matka, druhé nevlastní otec
data.description: Dvě sestry, dvě selhání ledvin a dva dárci v jedné rodině. Evě darovala ledvinu její matka, Kateřině o šest let později nevlastní otec. Právě transplantace od žijících dárců přitom podle odborníků přinášejí pacientům lepší výsledky a mohou jim ušetřit roky na dialýze. Často jim ale stojí v cestě obava otevřít téma dárcovství před svými blízkými.

data.title: Evropský Karibik nebo „Ďábelský ostrov“? Sardinií otřásá přetížená věznice mafiánů
data.description: Autobusový konvoj se zatemněnými okny projížděl o prvním zářijovém víkendu pod silným policejním dohledem uzavřenými uličkami hlavního města Sardinie. Do nového křídla věznice Uta s nejvyšší ostrahou převážel důležitý náklad – 88 notorických mafiánských bossů a jiných teroristů. Místní proti rozhodnutí protestují, podle nich představuje bezpečnostní riziko a ještě více zatíží věznice, které již nyní trpí nedostatkem personálu.

data.title: Pacient pod dohledem i doma. Lázně chtějí rehabilitaci řídit podle dat, říká expert
data.description: Takzvaná telerehabilitace a využívaní moderních technologií v pooperační péči je v Česku na vzestupu. Fakultní nemocnice Brno, Fakulta biomedicínského inženýrství ČVUT a lázeňská skupina Royal Spa nově testují digitální platformu, která spojí nemocnici, lázně i obývák pacienta do jednoho datového celku. „Lékaři i terapeuti tak poprvé uvidí průběh léčby v reálném čase,“ říká v rozhovoru pro iDNES.cz Aleš Příhoda, zdravotní ředitel lázeňské skupiny Royal Spa, kam spadají třeba termální lázně Velké Losiny nebo Luhačovice.

data.title: Chtěli šály soupeřů. Za loupež musí platit desetitisíce a hokej naživo dlouho neuvidí
data.description: Jedna podmínka, peněžité tresty v rozmezí 18 až 27 tisíc korun a nejméně na rok a půl zákaz návštěvy ligových hokejových utkání. S takovým trestem od soudu odešlo šest fanoušků Dukly, kteří po lednovém utkání v Jihlavě napadli příznivce Slavie Praha. Chtěli se zmocnit jejich šál a klubových symbolů.

data.title: Do Kyjeva jela i bez Sněmovny. Brání nás i zbytek Evropy, řekla Urbanová
data.description: Místopředsedkyně Sněmovny Barbora Urbanová z hnutí STAN se vypravila do Kyjeva, i když její cestu dříve hlasy poslanců vládní koalice ANO, SPD a Motoristů sobě neschválil organizační výbor české dolní komory parlamentu. „Žijete tady obyčejný život a najednou vám nad hlavou proletí dron. Já to už dneska vím, protože jsem tady,“ řekla Urbanová ve videu z Kyjeva.

data.title: Je libo se nechat pohřbít v rybě nebo injekční stříkačce? Rakve vyprávějí příběhy
data.description: V Ghaně může i rakev vyprávět příběh člověka, který v ní spočine. Hudebník odpočívá v obří kytaře, učitel v peru a rybář třeba v kánoi. Figurativní rakve tam nejsou jen bizarní kuriozitou, ale osobitým způsobem, jak se rozloučit se zesnulým – a zároveň mu ještě naposledy vzdát hold tím, co ho za života nejvíc vystihovalo. Někdo je schopen zvolit injekční stříkačku pro zesnulého lékaře.

data.title: 5 το πρωί ΔΕΘ Edition: «Συμβόλαιο τιμής» με 7 νομοσχέδια από τον Ανδρουλάκη
data.description: Επτά νομοσχέδια για τους πρώτους έξι μήνες μιας κυβέρνησης ΠαΣοΚ παρουσίασε ως «συμβόλαιο τιμής» ο Νίκος Ανδρουλάκης. Από τον 13ο μισθό και τη 13η σύνταξη μέχρι το φθηνότερο ρεύμα, την κατάργηση των τεκμηρίων και τις παρεμβάσεις για ακρίβεια, στέγη και οικογένεια, ξεδίπλωσε το σχέδιό του για «πολιτική αλλαγή». Και απέναντι στην κυβέρνηση ανέβασε τους τόνους: από το «Μητσοτάκης ή χάος», όπως είπε, περάσαμε στο «Μητσοτάκης ή Ερντογάν». Σήμερα η συνέντευξη Τύπου.

data.title: Minim Martap : au-delà des divergences financières, l’atout industriel d’A2MP pour relancer la bauxite camerounaise
data.description: © A2MP Le feuilleton autour du principal gisement de bauxite camerounais Minim Martap continue. Ce vendredi 11 septembre, A2MP Investments a apporté de nouvelles précisions face à Canyon Resources, qui recommande toujours à ses actionnaires de refuser son offre de rachat. Retour sur les enjeux de ce bras de fer pour le contrôle de ce qui devrait devenir la première mine de bauxite industrielle du Cameroun. Un projet majeur freiné par un désaccord entre actionnaires Il y a encore quelques mois, la presse camerounaise présentait Minim Martap comme l'un des projets miniers les plus prometteurs du pays, avec une première exportation de bauxite annoncée pour cette année. Fin juillet, la plateforme minière panafricaine A2MP (détentrice de 55,56 % de Canyon) a toutefois créé la surprise en proposant d’acquérir le reste du capital au prix de 0,05 AUD par action dans le cadre d’une offre publique d'achat hors marché. Tout part d'un désaccord sur la valeur du projet. Selon un rapport d'expert commandé par Canyon, l'offre d'A2MP sous-évaluerait le projet, notamment en négligeant des réserves de bauxite qui resteraient exploitables au-delà des vingt premières années. A2MP conteste ce calcul : le permis minier expire en 2044, et l'estimation de la part de Canyon dans le projet a elle-même beaucoup variée en quelques mois, passant d'environ 80 à 27 millions de dollars australiens. En février 2026, l’expert indépendant évaluait la valeur de la participation de Canyon Resources dans le projet entre 45 et 115 millions de dollars australiens, avec 80 millions comme estimation la plus probable. Cette valeur n’est plus que de 27 millions six mois plus tard. Pour A2MP, cette variation illustre les limites d’une valorisation qu’elle juge particulièrement sensible aux hypothèses retenues. Autre désaccord entre les deux parties : Canyon estime désormais la valeur du projet à 538 millions de dollars, contre 521 millions auparavant, soit une hausse de 17 millions. Pour A2MP, cette progression ne reflète toutefois pas une amélioration réelle du projet. Elle s’expliquerait principalement par la modification de la période prise en compte dans le calcul. À méthode comparable, cette valeur aurait au contraire diminué d’environ 33 millions de dollars. Dans une communication rendue publique le 11 septembre, A2MP déclare que son offre de 0,05 dollar australien par action est définitive et ne sera pas revalorisée en l'absence d'une contre-offre concurrente. Le groupe Panafricain confirme dans le même temps que son offre ne sera pas prolongée au-delà du 21 septembre à 19h. A2MP indique enfin détenir désormais, avec ses associés, un intérêt de 56,63 % du capital de Canyon. Le groupe, déjà premier actionnaire de Canyon, rappelle son intention de continuer à jouer un rôle constructif dans l'avenir de la société, quelle que soit l'issue de l'offre. Ce bras de fer dépasse toutefois la seule question financière. Pour le Cameroun, Minim Martap représente l'entrée du pays dans la production de bauxite, avec à la clé des milliers d’emplois et des revenus miniers importants attendus depuis plusieurs années. Chaque mois de blocage retarde cette perspective. Un actionnaire doté à la fois des moyens financiers et de l'expérience industrielle n'aurait-il pas plus de chances de le faire enfin décoller ? A2MP, l’expertise d’un poid lourd panafricain Présente dans neuf pays africains, la plateforme panafricaine A2MP associe à la fois l'extraction et la transformation locale de minéraux critiques comme l'or, la bauxite, le manganèse et le minerai de fer. La plateforme revendique un portefeuille d’une dizaine d’actifs miniers et quatre pôles de traitement. Ce modèle unique sur le continent a reçu le soutien de FEDA, bras d'investissement d'Afreximbank, qui a engagé 300 millions de dollars pour accélérer son déploiement, saluant un modèle capable de retenir davantage de valeur sur le continent. Sur le terrain, A2MP revendique sa capacité à faire avancer rapidement des projets d’ampleur. En Sierra Leone, FG Gold, dont A2MP détient près de la moitié du capital, développe le projet aurifère de Baomahun, l'un des plus importants du continent avec 5,81 millions d'onces de ressources. La première mine d’or commerciale à grande échelle du pays doit créer jusqu’à 900 emplois directs et indirects et peser  10 % au PIB national. Au Gabon, Nouvelle Gabon Mining, une autre société du portefeuille, exploite deux mines de manganèse d'une capacité de 2 millions de tonnes par an. Face à un projet qui accumule les retards, la question posée aux actionnaires de Canyon dépasse le seul prix proposé : elle touche aussi à la capacité de chaque partie à faire sortir le projet Minim Martap de terre. Pour le Cameroun, qui a besoin de partenaires fiables pour concrétiser ses projets miniers stratégiques, une résolution rapide du différend reste la condition pour transformer ce gisement en emplois et en revenus. À la différence d'un actionnaire purement financier, A2MP peut mobiliser à la fois des capitaux internationaux, une expertise panafricaine  éprouvée et des relais institutionnels solides, comme le montre le soutien d'Afreximbank. Reste à confirmer si l’entreprise réussira à gagner cet ambitieux pari et convaincre la majorité des actionnaires de sa capacité à redresser ce projet clé pour l’avenir du Cameroun. Cet article Minim Martap : au-delà des divergences financières, l’atout industriel d’A2MP pour relancer la bauxite camerounaise est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Affaire motocycliste tué à Matadi : un commissaire de police condamné à 5 ans de prison

data.title: Ebola à Djugu: trois cas confirmés au site de déplacés de la plaine de Savo
data.description: Trois cas confirmés de la maladie à virus Ebola ont été enregistrés au site de déplacés de la plaine de Savo, dans le territoire de Djugu, en Ituri. Ce site accueille plus de 70 000 personnes dans des conditions de vie précaires, marquées par une forte promiscuité, un accès limité aux services de base et des dispositifs de prévention insuffisants. Une situation qui fait craindre une propagation rapide de l’épidémie.

data.title: CAF Champions League : TP Mazembe domine Medeama et se qualifie pour le deuxième tour
data.description: Le Tout Puissant Mazembe a validé son billet pour le deuxième tour préliminaire de la CAF Champions League après sa victoire convaincante face au Medeama SC du Ghana, sur le score de 3‑1, lors du match retour disputé ce samedi. Les Corbeaux de Lubumbashi ont rapidement pris les commandes grâce à Patrick Mwaungulu, auteur de l’ouverture du score dès la 3ᵉ minute. À la 19ᵉ minute, Kazema a doublé la mise, permettant aux Congolais de regagner les vestiaires avec un avantage confortable de 2‑0.

data.title: CAF‑C2 : le DC Virunga de Goma à Pretoria pour affronter Bazar Brothers
data.description: Le DC Virunga de Goma est arrivé à Pretoria (Afrique du Sud) pour affronter les Bazar Brothers des Seychelles, ce dimanche 13 septembre 2026. data.title: Université de Kisangani : 1 600 étudiants sans abri après l’incendie de l’intendance universitaire
data.description: Un incendie survenu dans la nuit du 12 septembre a ravagé l’intendance de l’Université de Kisangani, laissant environ 1 600 étudiants sans abri. Les pertes matérielles sont considérables et l’origine du sinistre reste inconnue. Le maire de l’intendance, Chrispin Gbiande Bengangba, lance un SOS aux autorités pour venir en aide aux étudiants.

data.title: Les coupures d’électricité à Kinsuka‑Pêcheur perturbent les ménages et les petits commerces
data.description: Depuis plus d’un mois, les habitants du quartier Kinsuka‑Pêcheur, dans la commune de Ngaliema, vivent au rythme des coupures répétées d’électricité. Cette situation affecte profondément les activités quotidiennes des ménages et fragilise les revenus des petits commerçants. Dans plusieurs quartiers, l’électricité n’est disponible que quelques jours par semaine.

data.title: Ericsson celebrates 150 years of global innovation, 30 years of partnership and digital transformation in Ghana
data.description: Rostand Njomgang, Head of Cluster Central Ericsson West and Southern Africa, says: “For 150 years, Ericsson has been driven by the idea that communication can change the world. In Ghana, we have seen this become a reality. Our technology has helped bridge distances, empower entrepreneurs, and connect communities. As we look ahead, we are dedicated to advancing skills development and investing in the ecosystem that will support Ghana’s ambition to become a digital leader. The next chapter of connectivity, defined by 5G, AI, and cloud innovation, holds immense promise, and we are proud to be a partner in making it happen.”

data.title: Ghana’s Ambassador to Serbia hosts African ambassadors’ September meeting in Belgrade
data.description:
Ghana’s Ambassador to Serbia, Kwesi Ahwoi, has hosted the September 2026 meeting of the Group of African Ambassadors resident in Serbia.

The meeting, held at the Ghana Mission’s Residence in Belgrade, brought together African ambassadors and other diplomatic representatives stationed in Serbia to discuss issues of common interest to the African diplomatic community.

The regular gathering provides a platform for African diplomatic missions in Serbia to exchange views on developments affecting the continent and explore opportunities for closer cooperation.

data.title: Ghana closer to terrorism threat than ever before – WACCE
data.description:
The West Africa Centre for Counter-Extremism (WACCE) has warned that Ghana faces a growing terrorism threat as extremist violence spreads across the Sahel and closer to the country’s borders.

The Centre says Ghana’s geographical proximity to countries experiencing increasing extremist attacks, coupled with internal socioeconomic challenges, could make the country more vulnerable to violent extremism.

Speaking at a 9/11 Memorial Dialogue in Accra on Thursday, September 11, WACCE Executive Director Mutaru Mumuni Muqthar said Ghana was now “closer to the threat” than ever before.

data.translatedDescription:
The West Africa Centre for Counter-Extremism (WACCE) has warned that Ghana faces a growing terrorism threat as extremist violence spreads across the Sahel and closer to the country’s borders.

The Centre says Ghana’s geographical proximity to countries experiencing increasing extremist attacks, coupled with internal socioeconomic challenges, could make the country more vulnerable to violent extremism.

Speaking at a 9/11 Memorial Dialogue in Accra on Thursday, September 11, WACCE Executive Director Mutaru Mumuni Muqthar said Ghana was now “closer to the threat” than ever before.

data.title: Refreshed PMP® certification reflects evolving demands of project delivery and the skills employers need
data.description:
AI continues to change the workplace, automating tasks, transforming established ways of working, and forcing a rethink of the skills employers need. As technology takes on more tasks and new tools emerge, technical skills are becoming outdated more quickly, with roughly half potentially obsolete within five years. For project professionals, the urgency to diversify their skill sets beyond technical knowledge has never been greater. 

It is against this backdrop that Project Management Institute (PMI) introduced a refreshed Project Management Professional (PMP)® certification exam in July 2026, continuing the certification’s evolution alongside the profession and the changing demands placed on project professionals.

data.title: Diaspora, du devoir au désir
data.description: Convoquée partout, la diaspora malagasy reste pensée comme une ressource à capter : transferts, compétences, investissements. Une question manque : pourquoi aurait-elle envie de le faire ? Une diaspora n'est pas héréditaire ; elle se reconstruit à chaque génération, et l'envie ne se décrète pas. À la veille des Assises Nationales de la Diplomatie Malagasy, plaidoyer pour passer du devoir au désir : donner aux nouvelles générations une bonne raison de rester dans la famille. L'invitation (…) - Editorial

Face aux interrogations suscitées par des informations faisant état de comptes vidés après leur saisie, le ministère de la Justice est sorti de son silence ce mercredi 9 septembre. data.title: Universidades de España y Europa mantienen proyectos con entidades israelíes vinculadas a defensa pese a anunciar su boicot académico
data.description: Al comienzo del curso académico, hace un año, el rector de la Universidad de Granada dirigió un mensaje de bienvenida a los estudiantes y miembros del personal docente. Pedro Mercado Pacheco subrayó que la universidad debía seguir siendo “un espacio para el diálogo, la reflexión crítica [...] la defensa de los derechos humanos y la construcción de la paz”. En aquel momento, los ataques contra Gaza arreciaban y la universidad estaba librando su propia batalla en los tribunales para defender su decisión de suspender su colaboración con ciertas entidades israelíes. El caso ha llegado al Tribunal Supremo, tras una larga batalla judicial con ACOM (Acción y Comunicación sobre Oriente Medio), un lobby proisraelí que desde el primer momento ha tratado de impedir que la decisión de la Universidad de Granada prospere. No se espera una sentencia hasta el próximo año, pero será de gran calado. El fallo puede tener implicaciones más allá de Granada y sentar un precedente sobre si las universidades españolas pueden invocar la defensa del derecho internacional y los derechos humanos a la hora de adoptar decisiones de colaboración internacional. Desde que las universidades españolas anunciaron en mayo de 2024 su decisión de suspender relaciones con las entidades israelíes  » The post Universidades de España y Europa mantienen proyectos con entidades israelíes vinculadas a defensa pese a anunciar su boicot académico first appeared on Cubadebate .

data.title: Tabla posiciones tras triunfo de Motagua; así quedan Olimpia y Marathón
data.description: La fecha 7 del torneo Apertura 2026 de la Liga Nacional continuó este sábado 12 de septiembre con dos atractivos compromisos. En el primer turno se midieron Olancho FC ante Real España , mientras que la jornada cerró con el choque entre Motagua y Génesis FC. En el Estadio Juan Ramón Brevé, los Potros evitaron el tropiezo gracias a un golazo de tiro libre de Ofir Padilla al minuto 90, decretando el 1-1 definitivo ante una Máquina que se había adelantado en el marcador con un tanto de Eddie Hernández. Posteriormente, las Águilas y el conjunto de Fernando Mira protagonizaron un intenso duelo que terminó con triunfo por la mínima (1-0) a favor del Ciclón Azul. Esta victoria le permite al vigente campeón reencontrarse con el triunfo y dar un salto en la clasificación. Con estos tres duelos disputados, el Real España asume provisionalmente el liderato del torneo al llegar a 15 unidades, manteniéndose invicto con cuatro victorias y tres empates. La aurinegra deja por detrás a Olimpia y Marathón (ambos con 14 puntos), clubes que se enfrentarán este domingo en una nueva edición del clásico que podría redefinir la cima. Por su parte, el Motagua escaló hasta el cuarto puesto tras sumar una victoria importante y llegar a los 13 puntos, desplazando a la quinta casilla al conjunto 'canino', que se quedó estancado en 10 unidades. En la sexta posición acecha de cerca el Olancho FC , con la misma cantidad de puntos. En la séptima plaza se sitúa Estrella Roja con 9 unidades, producto de su empate 2-2 del viernes frente a Platense. El Independiente marcha octavo con 6 puntos antes de su cruce dominical contra Juticalpa FC, mientras que el "Tiburón" es noveno con 5. Cierran la tabla CD Choloma en el décimo lugar (4 pts) a la espera de su visita a los Lobos de la UPNFM, Juticalpa en la penúltima casilla con 3 unidades y, en el fondo, la UPNFM con apenas 2 puntos, siendo el único equipo que aún no conoce la victoria en el certamen. - Estrella Roja 2-2 Platense - Olancho FC 1-1 Real España - Motagua 1-0 Génesis FC - Lobos UPNFM vs CD Choloma (Domingo 13 de septiembre, 3:00 p. m.) - Marathón vs Olimpia (Domingo 13 de septiembre, 5:15 p. m.) - Independiente vs Juticalpa FC (Domingo 13 de septiembre, 7:30 p. m.)

data.title: Joven es acusada de hacerse pasar por miembro del cártel del “Diablo” para extorsionar
data.description: San Pedro Sula, Cortés . Una joven hondureña, señalada de presuntamente extorsionar a comerciantes y residentes de Yoro y San Pedro Sula haciéndose pasar por integrante del denominado cártel del "Diablo” fue capturada este sábado en la colonia La Aurora de San Pedro Sula, Cortés. La detenida fue identificada como Carla Verónica Chirinos Perdomo , de 25 años, originaria de San Juan, Yoro, y residente en la colonia La Aurora. En el ámbito criminal, según el informe policial, era conocida con el alias de “ La Morena ”. De acuerdo con Equipos de la División Anti Extorsión y Asociaciones Terroristas (DAET), la mujer se hacía pasar por integrante de la estructura criminal denominada cártel del "Diablo” con el propósito de generar temor entre sus víctimas y concretar cobros de extorsión. La Policía señala que Chirinos Perdomo tenía como función la recolección de dinero producto de las extorsiones en sectores de Yoro y San Pedro Sula, donde presuntamente mantenía bajo intimidación a comerciantes y residentes. Según el informe final de la DAET-SPS, la detenida exigía a sus víctimas cantidades que llegaban hasta un millón de lempiras, siempre utilizando el nombre de la organización criminal . Además, de acuerdo con la información policial, también solicitaba vehículos como parte de los cobros extorsivos. La captura se produjo a las 2:20 de la tarde del sábado, luego de una operación de vigilancia y seguimiento desarrollada por los equipos de la DAET en la colonia La Aurora, donde fue localizada y detenida la sospechosa. Durante el procedimiento, los agentes decomisaron una nota de extorsión y un teléfono celular marca Samsung, color gris, que presuntamente era utilizado para realizar las exigencias a las víctimas. También le encontraron 2,000 lempiras en efectivo, en cuatro billetes de 500 lempiras, además de una pistola de plástico, tipo juguete y de color negro, que habría sido utilizada para amedrentar a las personas a quienes exigía los pagos. La investigación señala como perjuicio a un testigo protegido, cuya identidad no fue revelada. La DAET indicó que el caso está relacionado con el delito de extorsión y que la detenida será puesta a disposición de las autoridades competentes para continuar el proceso correspondiente. Con la captura de alias “ La Morena ”, los equipos de la DAET buscan avanzar en el esclarecimiento de las actividades extorsivas atribuidas a la detenida y determinar si existen otras personas involucradas en los cobros realizados en Yoro y San Pedro Sula.

data.title: Video muestra momentos previos al ataque contra los hermanos en Santa Rita, Copán
data.description: Santa Rita, Copán . Una nueva grabación difundida en redes sociales muestra los momentos previos al ataque armado en el que murieron los hermanos Lito y Miguel Cuestas, en el sector de El Campamento, municipio de Santa Rita, Copán. Las víctimas fueron identificadas por sus familiares como Lito Cuestas y Miguel Cuestas , originarios de la comunidad de Las Mesas. Ambos fueron atacados a disparos por sujetos armados, de acuerdo con los reportes conocidos sobre el hecho. El doble crimen habría ocurrido en las inmediaciones de un establecimiento comercial y, según una de las versiones preliminares, los hermanos se encontraban dentro de un taller cuando fueron atacados. Sus cuerpos quedaron a la orilla de la carretera internacional CA-11. Las imágenes de una cámara de seguridad captaron parte de lo ocurrido. En la grabación se observa a un hombre acercarse al lugar donde se encontraban las víctimas y posteriormente huir, aunque las circunstancias que rodearon el ataque todavía deben ser establecidas mediante las investigaciones correspondientes. data.title: Docentes regresarán a las aulas el viernes 18 de septiembre en Honduras
data.description: Tegucigalpa, Honduras . La Secretaría de Educación informó que los docentes de todos los centros educativos del país reanudarán las actividades académicas con normalidad el viernes 18 de septiembre de 2026, luego de los desfiles patrios y los asuetos concedidos por las fiestas patrias y el Día del Maestro. El calendario establecido por la Secretaría contempla varias jornadas relacionadas con las celebraciones del 205 aniversario de la Independencia de Honduras. El lunes 14 de septiembre se desarrollarán las actividades preparatorias para los desfiles y actos culturales programados en cada centro educativo. Para el martes 15 de septiembre están previstos los desfiles patrios y actos culturales en los centros educativos, como parte de las actividades conmemorativas por los 205 años de Independencia de Honduras. Posteriormente, el miércoles 16 de septiembre se concederá asueto a todo el personal docente, según lo establecido en el comunicado oficial. La medida fue anunciada como un reconocimiento a la labor y participación de los maestros en la organización y desarrollo de las actividades cívicas. El jueves 17 de septiembre también será día libre para los docentes, debido al feriado establecido en conmemoración del Día del Maestro Hondureño . La Secretaría destacó la importancia del trabajo que realiza el magisterio en la formación integral de las nuevas generaciones. La principal aclaración del calendario corresponde al viernes 18 de septiembre . Ese día, los centros educativos de todo el país deberán reanudar sus actividades académicas con normalidad y continuar con el calendario escolar vigente. De esta manera, el período de actividades patrias y los días de descanso para el personal docente no se extenderá hasta el lunes 21 de septiembre. De acuerdo con la comunicación oficial, las clases y demás actividades académicas deberán retomarse el viernes 18. La Secretaría de Educación señaló que las disposiciones fueron adoptadas para garantizar la organización y participación de la comunidad educativa en las actividades cívicas conmemorativas de las fiestas patrias 2026 . La institución también reconoció el compromiso, dedicación, responsabilidad y espíritu cívico demostrado por los docentes durante la preparación y desarrollo de las actividades patrias. Con el retorno a las aulas el viernes 18 de septiembre, los centros educativos deberán dar continuidad al calendario escolar establecido. La Secretaría reiteró que estas actividades buscan fortalecer entre los estudiantes el amor a la patria, el respeto por los símbolos nacionales y los valores que identifican a Honduras.
